name: Nelson City Centre
tagline: Trafalgar Street, the cathedral steps and the Saturday market
description: The compact centre running up Trafalgar Street to the cathedral on its rise, with the shops, the restaurants and the Saturday market on Montgomery Square. The Maitai river runs along one edge and Queens Gardens sit beside it. Everything in Nelson that is not a beach or a mountain is within this ten-minute square.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the market, the cafes and the cathedral on foot
pros: Saturday market and all shops within ten minutes
Maitai river path for running from the door
cons: The highest rents in the town

name: Tahunanui
tagline: The beach suburb, with the long sand and the campground
description: Nelson's beach district southwest of the centre, built around a long shallow sand beach that is safe for swimming and busy through summer with domestic holidaymakers. Housing is a mix of older cottages and newer builds, and the airport is next door, which is convenient and audible on approach days.
bestFor: Stays that want the beach and are content with a bus into town
pros: Long safe swimming beach at the door
cons: Ten to fifteen minutes into the centre
Very busy over the summer holidays

name: The Wood and Britannia Heights
tagline: The hillside above the centre, with views over the bay
description: The slopes rising immediately behind the town, holding older villas, quiet streets and the Centre of New Zealand walk that climbs from Botanical Reserve to the geographic middle of the country. The views over Tasman Bay and the Boulder Bank are the best in the city and the centre is a short walk downhill.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a view and a quiet street five minutes above town
pros: Views over Tasman Bay and the mountains
Centre of New Zealand walk from the doorstep
Five to ten minutes downhill to the centre

name: Stoke and Richmond
tagline: The southern suburbs, where the value is
description: The residential belt running south towards Richmond, with supermarkets, schools, sports grounds and a settled population. It is ordinary suburban New Zealand and it is where rents fall meaningfully below the centre. The Great Taste Trail cycle route passes through, and the estuary and Rabbit Island are close.
bestFor: Longer stays where the rent matters more than the address
pros: The lowest rents in the Nelson area
Great Taste Trail cycle route through it
cons: Fifteen to twenty minutes into the centre
No character and nothing to walk to
Bus service is adequate rather than good

name: Motueka and the Abel Tasman Road
tagline: Towards the national park, orchards and the coast
description: The town an hour northwest along the coast, at the gateway to Abel Tasman and the Kahurangi trailheads, surrounded by apple orchards and hop gardens. It is smaller and cheaper than Nelson, has a strong alternative and artisan population, and is where anyone whose life is organised around the park would sensibly live.
bestFor: Stays built around Abel Tasman and Kahurangi rather than the city
pros: Abel Tasman and Kahurangi access from the doorstep
Cheaper than Nelson for a house
Strong local food and artisan scene
cons: An hour from Nelson and its services
